text:
Early compiles preferred GitHub folder names and original tweets. That dropped replies, dropped long X-only reports, and ranked recent gravity over April cosmology. The Hubble-tension miss was a scan-rule failure. The fix is a public log: which windows ran, which known threads were deferred, and the last ingested status URL.

10 Sep 2026 20:25 UTC — v12.41 moment-map closure (constraint algebra without spacetime). Status https://x.com/aaronspradlin/status/2098145800949776410. GitHub-only 12 Sep: ResearchHistory/UQCF-GEM latest completed v14.04 intertwiner stop, Pillar 3 OPEN. No X field note for v13–v14 — none invented. Gravity’s constraints not identified.

Month windows

Ingest rules (unchanged)

Scan from:@aaronspradlin month by month. Do not start from Tmp/TOE folder names.
Keep replies. A science claim under someone else’s thread is still a field note if it carries an equation, a named harness, a protocol verdict, or a correction.
Keep original long threads that are not GitHub packages.
Do not ingest every @grok one-liner. Industry / Luminaries posts stay off the science ledger.
Recompile is still batch, not live. New posts land when the atlas is rebuilt.

The how-to-read page already admits past scan-rule misses. This log is how the next miss becomes detectable.
